reasoning: iter-054: fuse cull + blend into a single outer pass over sorted_gaussian_ids that maintains 32 in-flight MbAccums (4 KB total — fits L1 easily) and a uint32_t saturation bitmap. Per Gaussian: read gauss_rec[g] once, apply directly to every corner-test-surviving microblock with a check against mb_saturated. Saturation refreshed every K=4 applies/mb to amortise the max_t_neon read-after-write barrier. Hypothesis: cuts ~4 random gauss_rec/colors reads per Gaussian = ~60 MB of memory traffic per frame. Result: REGRESSION. sum_total 255 -> 278.7 ms (+9%, +23 ms). blend stage 139 -> 161 ms (+16%). PSNR bit-identical (min 60.34 dB). Causes: (a) the per-application saturation-bitmap check (1u << m & mb_saturated) + the per-mb apply-count increment + the conditional max_t refresh together adds ~6 scalar ops on every inner (g, m) pair — the old per-microblock blend ran a tight kn-iteration loop where the compiler+OoO ran the apply_gaussian_neon body completely free of per-iteration control flow (other than the every-4 max_t barrier); (b) interleaved MbAccum access (next apply touches a DIFFERENT 128 B accum) defeats the OoO engine's ability to pipeline successive applies — in the old code, 4 sequential applies to the same accum had a clean store-forward dependency chain that the OoO could resolve in flight, but cross-mb interleaving forces 4× as many distinct LSU streams and the 4 NEON pipes can't reorder across them; (c) the gauss_rec memory savings were real (~2 ms wall) but smaller than expected because the L3 + DRAM are doing fine on the random ~9 MB working set under HW prefetching. Net: the inner-loop microarchitecture cost dominated. Reverting. Lesson: tile-scoped multi-accumulator interleaving must overlap apply pipelines (e.g., 2-deep instead of 32-deep) for the OoO engine to keep its store-forward chain intact.
